mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.1) or the rate increase is not sustained beyond the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 such triggered events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the S&P 500 20-day monthly baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy: GDPC1 ) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth rate > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 such demand acceleration events, the 5-day forward returns show no mean outperformance versus the S&P 500 5-day monthly baseline (mean ratio ≤ 1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) index below 98.0 for two consecutive months suggests supply-side weakness that reduces market capacity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 98.0 for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: supply shock or soft landing failure
failure_condition: During INDPRO contraction periods, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean 20-day return during expansion periods (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 7% for a month, the market anticipates a near-term rate hike, which compresses discount rates and lowers equity present value, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 7% in a single month
failure_condition: In 5 such episodes, the 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative relationship with the CPIAUCSL inflation spike (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% coinciding with a decline in labor force participation (HOUST) signals a tight labor market that can drive wage growth and corporate hiring, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% while HOUST decreases by > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 10 triggered events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to the S&P 500 20-day monthly baseline (mean ratio ≤ 1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (PAYEMS) exceeding prior month by at least 3% indicate accelerating consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 3% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 15 such acceleration events, the 5-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive deviation from the S&P 500 5-day monthly mean (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below 450 million dollars for three consecutive months indicates a supply contraction that reduces production capacity, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 450 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During all such contraction phases, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the average 60-day return during expansion phases (p > 0.1).
